newsitem.title: USA: US Enrichment Q4 net hurt by customer changes.
newsitem.headline: US Enrichment Q4 net hurt by customer changes.

text.p: United States Enrichment Corp said on Friday that its fourth quarter, ended June 30 declined due primarily to changes in the timing of customer fuel requirements.

The company, which provides fuel enrichment services to electric utilities operating nuclear power plants, reported revenue of $421.0 million for the quarter, down from $446.0 million a year earlier. Net income declined to $82.4 million from $135.6 million a year earlier. USEC is a government corporation in the process of privatizing.
As a government corporation, it is exempt from federal, state and local income taxes.

During 1996, the company said, it changed to a June 30 fiscal year end from September 30 to more closely align with its natural business cycle. Results for fiscal 1995 have been restated to reflect the change in year end.

For fiscal 1996, USEC reported revenue of $1.41 billion compared with record revenue of $1.61 billion for the restated year ended June 30, 1995. Net income amounted to $304.1 million compared with record net income of $447.5 million a year earlier.
The lower revenue for the fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year 1996 was attributable primarily to changes in the timing of customer fuel requirements, the company said.

Customer requirements are determined by refueling schedules that generally range from 12 to 24 months and are affected by, among other things, the seasonal nature of electricity demand and production, it said.
The timing of customer reactor fuel reloads tends to be fairly predictable over the long run, but may impact quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year comparisons.

The decline in fourth quarter and year earnings resulted from lower revenue, increased spending on the Atomic Vapor Laser Isotope Separation process and higher unit production costs at the gaseous diffusion plants, USEC said.

It said the higher unit production costs were the result of lower production levels at the plants. Production levels declined at the gaseous diffusion plants as a result of increased maintenance activities, changes in regulatory requirements, and increased purchases of low enriched uranium from Russia. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
